newsitem.title: BELGIUM: City Hotels buys two U.S. hotels.
newsitem.headline: City Hotels buys two U.S. hotels.

text.p: Belgian leisure group City Hotels said on Wednesday it had bought two more hotels in the United States for a total of $11.75 million.
The Royce Hotel in Detroit has 257 rooms and the Radisson Hotel in Dayton has 186 rooms, the firm said in a statement.
It said that after modernisation and transformation costing $4.5 million, the Royce Hotel was expected to generate a gross annual cash flow of $2.4 million from March 1998.
Likewise, after spending $5.6 million on converting the Radisson Hotel it was expected to generate a gross annual cash flow of $1.6 million from April 1998.
City Hotels said the purchases were part of its strategic plan for the United States.
A third hotel, the Radisson Resort at Singer Island in Florida was in the process of acquisition for a price including the cost of modernisation of $12.5 million.
This hotel is expected to generate a gross annual cash flow of $2 million after conversion into a 202-room Sheraton.
The firm said letter of intent had been signed regarding the purchase of three other hotels -- one at Charlotte, North Carolina, and two at Saint Louis -- for a total investment of $31 million.
The three hotels have between them 527 rooms.
